projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 53.0 y over a 13-day collection window (226 samples, 200 'people', age and date both route R1). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values in this project.
projects.cause: The BioSample attribute Subject_ID is a participant number assigned within each village, not a study-wide person id, so the same string denotes different people in different villages. Subject_ID '2015_12' is carried by a 60-year-old woman in Mosenahanha, a 17-year-old in Washudihanha and a 7-year-old in Kuyuwininha. Across the 2,157 BioSamples of the project, 100 of 347 distinct Subject_IDs span more than one Village and 59 span more than one Gender. Keying on Village+Subject_ID gives 527 groups, of which 0 have conflicting Gender and only 4 have more than one Age.
projects.correction_rule: person_key = Village + '|' + Subject_ID for PRJEB55648; Subject_ID alone is a per-village participant number and must not be used for person grouping (it is reused in every village). Age is the BioSample attribute 'Age' in whole years (x365.25).
projects.affected_samples: all catalogued samples of the project (study-wide re-key); concretely the 100 Subject_IDs that occur in more than one Village
projects.evidence_quote: Subject_ID="2015_12" Village="Mosenahanha" Age="60" Gender="F"  /  Subject_ID="2015_12" Village="Kuyuwininha" Age="7" Gender="F"
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample XML, SAMEA110758999 and SAMEA110758875 (PRJEB55648); www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/api/xml/
projects.note: No linked publication was found in Europe PMC for PRJEB55648, so the evidence is the archive records only. Village has 9 values including 'Visitors'.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 50.0 y with a 882-day collection span (384 samples, 328 'people'). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: Two problems, both on age. (1) SAMEA115100512 and SAMEA115100689 are demonstrably the same participant at two HNRC visits: they share 21 identical lifetime-history attributes (total_days_coc 1084, total_days_met 1323, total_quantity_pop 1058, nadir_cd4 300, first_pos_test_date 1987-09-09, ...) and their days_since_last_use_met (2553 -> 3226) and days_since_last_use_amp (5628 -> 6301) both advance by exactly 673 days, the gap between collection dates 2019-06-17 and 2021-04-20. Yet host_age is 20 at visit 120 and 72 at visit 144, so host_age=20 is a transcription error for roughly 70. (2) The catalogued age for SAMEA115100512 is 8,035 d = 22.0 y, which is not that sample's host_age (20) but equals its age_of_first_use_alc / age_of_first_use_mar / age_of_first_use_pop (=22); the study carries 11 'age_of_first_use_*' attributes (alc, mar, coc, met, pop, tos, tob, sed, mas, ant, amp) that are ages of first substance use, not age at collection.
projects.correction_rule: age_at_collection_days = 365.25 x host_age (identical to attribute 'age') for PRJEB38909; never match any attribute whose key starts with 'age_of_first_use' or contains 'age_at_diagnosis'. Then drop any host_age that conflicts with another sample of the same participant by more than the elapsed days between their collection dates (SAMEA115100512 host_age=20 vs SAMEA115100689 host_age=72, 673 days apart).
projects.affected_samples: SAMEA115100512 (host_age 20, true value approx 70) for the archive error; study-wide for the extractor rule -- 835 of 1,029 BioSamples carry a numeric host_age, the remainder have 'not applicable' or an empty value and are the ones where the age_of_first_use_* fallback can fire
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample XML, SAMEA115100512 and SAMEA115100689 (PRJEB38909, Qiita study 11135)
projects.note: The catalogued subject ids ('10509', 'F0164') do not appear anywhere in the ENA sample, run or experiment records, so the grouping itself could not be checked against the archive; the evidence above shows the two flagged samples really are one participant, which makes this an age error and not a grouping error. Europe PMC full text for the linked paper (PMID 42716144) returned HTTP 500 on three attempts.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 50.0 y with a 0-day collection span (127 samples, 48 'people'). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: host_subject_id D1, D2 and D3 are the three FMT stool donors, and their samples are the administered donor product units (titles 'FMT027_unit_Metagenomic_08162023' etc.). The host_age and host_sex written on those unit records are the RECIPIENT's, not the donor's: each unit's host_age equals exactly the host_age carried by the matching recipient's own samples (FMT027 -> 28, FMT029 -> 70, FMT030 -> 35, FMT031 -> 20, FMT032 -> 36), and host_sex flips with the recipient too (D1 and D2 units are both 'male' and 'female'). Donor D3 therefore looks like one person aged 20 to 70. The 24 donor-unit samples are D1 (10), D2 (9), D3 (5); the recipient subjects FMT001..FMT032 each have a single consistent age.
projects.correction_rule: in PRJNA1169096, for every sample whose host_subject_id is D1, D2 or D3 (sample title matches '<FMT###>_unit_'), clear age_at_collection_days and host sex -- these are the FMT recipient's values, and the donors' own ages are not stated anywhere in the record. Keep host_subject_id as the person key: D1-D3 genuinely are three donors.
projects.affected_samples: the 24 samples with host_subject_id D1, D2 or D3 (e.g. SAMN44065167, SAMN44065171, SAMN44065176, SAMN44065179, SAMN44065184); also SAMN44065058 (host_subject_id 'FMT', title 'FMT_Placebo_...', host_age 'missing')
projects.evidence_source: ENA/NCBI BioSample XML, SAMN44065171 and the FMT029 recipient samples (PRJNA1169096)
projects.note: Europe PMC full text for the trial paper (PMID 40460824, PMC12353604) returned HTTP 500 on three attempts and was not available from the PMC open-access bucket, so the donor/recipient reading rests on the archive records.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 44.4 y with a 781-day collection span (222 samples, 64 'people'). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values in the catalogued data.
projects.cause: A single sample carries a placeholder age of zero. SAMEA12565697 has age_years = host_age = 0.0 and age_cat 'baby', while its life_stage is 'Adult', its birth_year is 1975 and its host_subject_id hash is shared with four samples aged 44.3-44.4 y. Its collection_timestamp is '1975-06-09T17:30:00', i.e. the participant's date of birth was entered in the collection-date field and the age was then computed as 0. It is the only one of the 225 BioSamples with a pre-1990 collection_timestamp and the only one with age_cat 'baby'. The person grouping (a 128-hex host_subject_id) is sound: 67 subjects, none with conflicting birth_year or sex.
projects.correction_rule: in PRJEB50408 reject age_years/host_age == 0 when life_stage is 'Adult' or birth_year is before 2000; for SAMEA12565697 set age_at_collection_days to the value carried by the other samples of the same host_subject_id (approx 16,217 d = 44.4 y) or clear it, and never use its collection_timestamp 1975-06-09 as a collection date (it is the date of birth).
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample XML, SAMEA12565697 (PRJEB50408, Qiita study 13692)
projects.note: The catalogue already routes this sample's collection_date to the study-period reading '2019-06/2020-12' (R3), so the date is not affected; only the age is.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 39.0 y with no collection dates at all (6 samples, 3 'people'; age route R3, i.e. read from the paper). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: The BioSamples carry no age attribute whatsoever (only alias/title such as 'P2 stool before', organism Homo sapiens), so the catalogued ages were read from Table 1 of the paper, and they were taken from the wrong rows. Table 1 gives P1 20, P2 59, P3 16, P4 55, P5 57, P6 37, P7 34 years. The stored ages for patient P2 are 5,844 d (16.0 y, SAMEA4779313) and 20,089 d (55.0 y, SAMEA4779315) -- those are P3's and P4's ages, so the table rows were misaligned against the patient codes.
projects.correction_rule: re-map PRJEB27661 ages from the patient code in the sample alias ('P<n> stool before|1 week|1 month') to Table 1 of PMID 31727954: P1=20, P2=59, P3=16, P4=55, P5=57, P6=37, P7=34 years (x365.25 for days). Person key = the P<n> token of the alias; the alias 'Clostridium butyricum Miyairi 588' (SAMEA4779331) is a bacterial culture with no host and must carry no age.
projects.affected_samples: all 21 patient stool samples (7 patients x before / 1 week / 1 month); at minimum the samples of P2, and every other patient should be re-read because the offset is systematic
projects.evidence_quote: P2 Male 59 Short bowel syndrome after occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery
projects.evidence_source: Table 1 'Clinical characteristics of 7 SBT patients', Sci Rep 2019 9:16776, PMID 31727954 / PMC6856387, doi 10.1038/s41598-019-53173-7
projects.note: Sex in Table 1 (P1 F, P2 M, P3 F, P4 F, P5 M, P6 M, P7 F) can be used as a cross-check when re-reading. The study has no collection dates in the archive.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 37.9 y with a 0-day collection span (182 samples, 68 'people'; age route R2, dates route R1 and only year-resolution '2016'). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: Sample aliases encode MAMI_<family><B|M><timepoint><material>, where B is the infant, M the mother, H stool and BM breast milk. On the mother's milk samples the age that was captured is the time postpartum, not the mother's age: for mother 046M the stool sample MAMI_046M04H carries 13,879.5 d (38.0 y) while the milk sample MAMI_046M04BM carries 30 d, and the paper states that maternal milk was collected one month postpartum. 27 of the 182 BioSamples are milk (alias ending 'BM', timepoint 03 or 04); 32 are mother stool and 122 infant stool.
projects.correction_rule: in PRJEB74322 do not take the supplementary 'age' value for samples whose alias ends in 'BM' (mother's milk) -- it is days postpartum, not the donor's age. Either clear age_at_collection_days for those 27 samples or copy the mother's age from her matching MAMI_<family>M<timepoint>H stool sample. Person key = MAMI_<family><B|M> (B infant, M mother); that part of the grouping is correct.
projects.affected_samples: the 27 samples whose alias ends in 'BM', e.g. SAMEA115454951 (MAMI_046M04BM)
projects.evidence_quote: Maternal fecal and milk samples collected 1 month postpartum were also metagenomically sequenced to explore the contribution of these microbial sources in vertical mother-infant bacterial transmission.
projects.evidence_source: Cell Host & Microbe 2024, PMID 38870906 / PMC11183301, doi 10.1016/j.chom.2024.05.005 (MAMI cohort)
projects.note: The BioSamples themselves carry no age attribute (only organism, collection year and country), so the ages come from the supplementary table and could not be re-derived from the archive.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 35.0 y with a 365-day collection span (1,609 samples, 110 'people'; age routes R1 895 / R2 465). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: host_subject_id is family_id with a member digit appended: suffix '0' is the mother (host_life_stage 'adult', host_age_units 'years') and suffix '1' the infant ('infant', units 'days'). Every mother's BioSample also carries host_age_infant, the infant's age in days, and that is what was captured for the mother. For the flagged subject 123230 the stored ages are 2, 4, 7, 10, 14 and 21 days -- exactly the host_age_infant values on those records -- while each of those samples has host_age = 35 with host_age_units = 'years'. host_age equals host_age_mother on all 385 'adult' rows and host_age_infant on all 385 'infant' rows, so host_age plus host_age_units is the correct field; 515 of the 524 mother samples have host_age_infant different from host_age. The person grouping itself is sound.
projects.correction_rule: in PRJEB83236 take age from host_age interpreted with host_age_units; where host_age_units is absent (1,055 of 1,917 BioSamples) read the unit from the host_subject_id suffix -- years if it ends in '0' (mother), days if it ends in '1' (infant), equivalently host_life_stage adult/infant. Never read host_age_infant or host_age_mother as the sampled person's age.
projects.affected_samples: the 524 samples whose host_subject_id ends in '0' (mother/adult), e.g. SAMEA117484400, SAMEA117484418, SAMEA117484426, SAMEA117484433, SAMEA117484447, SAMEA117484455
projects.evidence_quote: host_life_stage="adult" host_age="35" host_age_units="years" host_age_mother="35" host_age_infant="21" infant_age="w3" family_id="12323" host_subject_id="123230"
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample XML, SAMEA117484400 (PRJEB83236, Qiita study 14834)
projects.note: Two infant-suffix rows (SAMEA117489709, SAMEA117489983, host_subject_id 123231) carry host_age 35 with no units; 35 days is plausible for an infant, so they are left alone, but they show that the unit-less block cannot be disambiguated by magnitude alone.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 35.0 y with a 410-day collection span (120 samples, 19 'people'). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: The 'host subject id' (CTOT03LG....) identifies a transplant pair, not a person. All 13 subject ids contain both 'Lung transplant recipient' samples and an 'Organ donor' sample, and in all 13 the two carry different host age (and usually different host sex and host disease): CTOT03LG13028 has a 54-year-old male recipient with Pulmonary Fibrosis and a 19-year-old donor with Head Trauma. The project holds 101 recipient samples, 13 organ-donor samples and 6 buffer/water controls.
projects.correction_rule: person_key for PRJNA419524 = host_subject_id + '|' + health_state; the 13 samples with health_state = 'Organ donor' are the lung donor and must not be grouped with the recipient who shares the host subject id. The 6 samples with no host attributes (titles 'Buffer', 'PCR NTC', 'Molecular Water', 'Extraction Buffer') are negative controls and should carry no person at all.
projects.affected_samples: the 13 organ-donor samples (one per subject id), e.g. SAMN08056593 under host subject id CTOT03LG13028
projects.evidence_quote: Bioproject PRJNA419524 contains sequencing files from BAL fluid obtained from donor lungs and recipients, the latter being monitored longitudinally
projects.evidence_source: Viruses 2024 16:953, PMID 38932245 / PMC11209621, doi 10.3390/v16060953; corroborated by BioSample health_state on SAMN08056592 vs SAMN08056593
projects.note: These are lung (BAL) and blood metagenomes, not gut; the donor BAL is the pre-implantation graft sample.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 34.0 y with no collection dates (210 samples, 168 'people'), plus one negative age (-32,142 d, SAMEA7731569).
projects.cause: Two independent faults. (1) Person grouping: the project carries two families of identifier attributes that disagree on three samples. SAMEA7731553 has subjectid = subject_id = '150675-86' but patient_id = host_subject_id = '150675-135' and patient_number = '135'; the same split occurs on SAMEA7731550 ('150675-111' vs '150675-143') and SAMEA7731429 ('150675-113' vs '150675-133'). Grouping the 194 dated samples by subjectid gives 153 groups with zero conflicting yob, whereas patient_id/host_subject_id gives 2 conflicting groups and patient_number 3. The flagged person '135' is in fact SAMEA7731553 (yob 4.9.1988, which matches SAMEA7731539 subjectid 150675-86, same first_patient_metadata_line 334) merged with SAMEA7731586 (yob 8.26.1954, subjectid 150675-135). (2) Negative age: SAMEA7731569 carries yob '8.13.2107' and host_age '-88'; the birth year is corrupt (it is the only one of 194 yob values outside 1900-2020).
projects.correction_rule: (a) use the attribute `subjectid` (identical to `subject_id`) as the person key for PRJEB42155 and ignore host_subject_id, patient_id and patient_number, which are wrong on SAMEA7731553, SAMEA7731550 and SAMEA7731429; where subjectid is 'Missing' fall back to patient_id. (b) Clear age for SAMEA7731569 because yob '8.13.2107' is not a valid birth year; if a value is needed, birth year = year(diagnosis_date) - age_at__diagnosis = 2000 - 23 = 1977.
projects.affected_samples: grouping: SAMEA7731553, SAMEA7731550, SAMEA7731429 (3 samples); negative age: SAMEA7731569 (1 sample)
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample XML, SAMEA7731553 and SAMEA7731569 (PRJEB42155, Qiita study 12675)
projects.note: host_age in this study is computed against a fixed metadata freeze (yob 1954 -> host_age 65, yob 1988 -> 31), not against the collection date, so host_age should be recomputed from yob and the sample's procedure_date / clinic_visit_date if a date-accurate age is wanted.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 34.0 y with a 1,096-day collection span (535 samples, 60 'people'; age route R2, dates year-only R1). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: One sample's age contradicts the subject's own label. Every sample title names the subject and its age group, and all ten W-2 samples read 'Fecal microbiome subject W-2 (adult) time N'; the paper also lists W-2 among the adult women who were breast-feeding during the sampling period. Yet the stored age for SAMEA120472561 (alias W-2_5, collected 2017) is 1,096 d = 3.0 y, while the subject's other nine samples are 12,784-13,514 d (35.0-37.0 y). The BioSamples carry no age attribute, so this is a bad row in the supplementary table the ages were read from.
projects.correction_rule: gate PRJEB101630 ages against the age group in the sample title: '(adult)' >= 18 y, '(adolescent)' 8-20 y, '(toddler)' < 4 y; on failure replace the value by interpolation from the same subject's other timepoints or clear it. For SAMEA120472561 (W-2_5, 2017) the interpolated value is about 13,149 d (36 y), not 1,096 d.
projects.affected_samples: SAMEA120472561 (W-2_5); the title-vs-age gate should be run over all 535 samples (313 adult, 101 adolescent, 121 toddler)
projects.evidence_quote: samples from women who were breast-feeding during part of the sampling period (W-1, W-2, W-3, W-9, and W-10) were incorporated into the analyses
projects.note: The paper reports starting mean ages of 41.6 y (adults, n=35), 11.9 y (adolescents, n=13) and 20 months (toddlers, n=12); W-2's exact age is in Supplementary Table S1, which was not retrieved, so the replacement value above is interpolated rather than quoted.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 32.0 y with no collection dates (93 samples, 92 'people'). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: host_subject_id is a short running number that is not unique across the cohort. host_subject_id '53' is carried by two different patients -- tube_id 'PDA_resected_CP_PDA037_R_META' (host_age 72) and tube_id 'Cyst_PDAKS211_R_meta' (host_age 40) -- and host_subject_id '30' likewise covers PDA019 (76, female) and PDAMN126 (77, male). Keying on the patient code embedded in tube_id / sample title gives 58 groups with no age conflict, against 88 host_subject_id groups of which 3 have conflicting ages and 1 conflicting sex.
projects.correction_rule: person_key for PRJEB59450 = the patient code parsed from tube_id or the sample title (regex PDA[A-Z]*[0-9]+, e.g. PDA037, PDAKS211, PDA019, PDAMN126), not host_subject_id; host_subject_id 53 and 30 each cover two different patients.
projects.affected_samples: the 4 samples under host_subject_id '53' (SAMEA112450513, SAMEA112450549) and '30'

projects.note: No publication for PRJEB59450 was found in Europe PMC, so the evidence is the archive records only.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 31.0 y with no usable collection dates (all samples carry 'collection date' = '2008/2010'); 396 samples, 330 'people'; age route R2. No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: The Spanish MetaHIT samples carry two batch prefixes, V1. and O2., over one shared patient register, so merging V1.UC38 with O2.UC38 is correct: V1 covers UC1-UC62 and CD1-CD42 while O2 covers 49 UC codes, 45 of them also in V1 and four (UC20, UC22, UC59, UC60) absent from V1 -- the pattern of one register sequenced in overlapping subsets, not of two independently numbered cohorts. The ages, read from a supplementary table, disagree across the batches: 8,766 d (24.0 y) on V1.UC38-0 against 20,088.75 d (55.0 y) on O2.UC38-0 and O2.UC38-2. The BioSamples carry no age, sex or subject attribute at all, so the archive cannot adjudicate, and the source table (Nielsen et al. 2014) is not open access -- Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar, PMC and Crossref TDM all returned no full text.
projects.correction_rule: keep the current person grouping for PRJEB1220 (strip the V1./O2. batch prefix and the trailing -<timepoint>: V1.UC38-0, O2.UC38-0 and O2.UC38-2 are one patient). Where the V1 and O2 rows of the same patient code give ages differing by more than the sampling interval, clear age_at_collection_days for that patient pending re-extraction from the Nielsen 2014 supplementary table; all samples share the collection date '2008/2010', so no interval can justify a multi-year gap.
projects.affected_samples: subject UC38 (SAMEA2042575, SAMEA2042994, SAMEA2042995); the same V1-vs-O2 comparison should be run over the 45 UC codes that appear in both batches
projects.evidence_quote: alias="V1.UC38-0" title="Stool sample from spanish" collection date="2008/2010"  /  alias="O2.UC38-0" title="Stool sample from spanish" collection date="2008/2010"
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample XML, SAMEA2042575 and SAMEA2042994 (PRJEB1220, MetaHIT-MGS); source metadata table is Nielsen et al., Nat Biotechnol 2014, doi 10.1038/nbt.2939, PMID 24997787 (closed access)
projects.note: Provisional: which of the two ages (24 y or 55 y) is correct could not be established because the source supplementary table is paywalled and the archive holds no age attribute. The grouping conclusion (V1 and O2 share one patient register) is inferred from the code-range pattern, not stated in a retrieved source.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 27.0 y with a 0-day collection span (134 samples, 112 'people'; age route R2, dates year-only '2017'). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: The BioSamples hold no age attribute, so the ages come from a supplementary table and were joined to the wrong rows. Sample names are AS<nnnn> or HC<nnn> plus a trailing A/B letter and an optional follow-up token (AS0001A baseline with AS0001-24MA; AS0083B baseline with AS0083-12MA). No AS code carries both a bare 'A' and a bare 'B' baseline (49 A-lettered and 26 B-lettered AS baselines, all 22 HC baselines B-lettered), so the letter marks a metadata/sequencing block rather than a second patient, and AS0083B and AS0083-12MA are the same patient twelve months apart. Their stored ages are 18,262.5 d (50.0 y) and 8,400.75 d (23.0 y), which cannot both be right.
projects.correction_rule: keep the person grouping (strip the trailing A/B letter and the follow-up token: AS0083B and AS0083-12MA are one patient). Re-key the supplementary age table on the full 'Sample name' including the A/B letter rather than on the bare patient number, and clear age_at_collection_days wherever two samples of one patient disagree by more than the follow-up interval.
projects.affected_samples: at minimum AS0083 (SAMEA5054141, SAMEA5054193); re-check the 8 codes whose baseline is B-lettered and follow-up A-lettered -- AS0036, AS0059, AS0062, AS0064, AS0069, AS0072, AS0080, AS0083 -- since those are where a per-letter-block row key would mis-join
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample XML, SAMEA5054141 and SAMEA5054193 (PRJEB29373); cohort described in Zhou et al., J Autoimmun 2020 107:102360, PMID 31806420 (closed access, no PMCID)
projects.note: Provisional: the source supplementary table is in a closed-access paper that Europe PMC does not hold, so which age is correct could not be established. The reading of the A/B letter as a batch marker rather than a second patient rests on the archive naming pattern, not on a retrieved statement.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 27.0 y with a 0-day collection span (219 samples, 144 'people'; all values route R1). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: The 'Patient ID' attribute is unique only within a disease cohort. 47 of the 106 Patient IDs occur in both the NSCLC and the RCC sample sets with a different 'host age', and 23 of them with a different 'host sex': Patient ID I_052 is a 70-year-old male with NSCLC on alias NSCLC_I_052_T0 and a 43-year-old male with RCC on alias RCC_I_052_T0. Keying on the disease prefix of the sample alias plus Patient ID gives 153 groups with zero conflicting age or sex, against 106 Patient ID groups of which 46 have conflicting ages.
projects.correction_rule: person_key for PRJEB22863 = the disease prefix of the sample alias (NSCLC or RCC, i.e. the text before the first underscore) + '|' + the 'Patient ID' attribute; Patient ID alone is reused between the two cohorts for 47 of 106 ids. The alias also carries the timepoint (T0, T1, T2), which is not part of the person key.
projects.affected_samples: the samples of the 47 Patient IDs present in both cohorts (e.g. I_001 to I_052, B_001); 118 NSCLC and 101 RCC samples in total
projects.evidence_quote: alias="NSCLC_I_052_T0" Patient ID="I_052" host age="70" host disease status="NSCLC"  /  alias="RCC_I_052_T0" Patient ID="I_052" host age="43" host disease status="RCC"
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample XML, SAMEA104416197 and SAMEA104416334 (PRJEB22863)
projects.note: 'Cohort' (discovery/validation) is a separate attribute and is not the discriminator; the discriminator is the tumour type, available from the alias prefix and from 'host disease status'.

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 21.1 y with a 0-day collection span (9 samples, 6 'people'; all values route R1). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: The study is cross-sectional: 9 BioSamples, one stool sample per participant, with the 'ID' attribute running 1-9 (HF-1 to HF-5 are ID 1-5, 'People living with HIV'; CF-1 to CF-4 are ID 6-9, 'Healthy Control'). The person key was taken from the number after the hyphen in the sample alias, so HF-1 (ID 1, age 49) and CF-1 (ID 6, age 70) were merged into one person, as were HF-2/CF-2, HF-3/CF-3 and HF-4/CF-4. No participant should have more than one sample.
projects.correction_rule: person_key for PRJNA1300398 = the BioSample 'ID' attribute (1-9), or equivalently the full sample alias (HF-1..HF-5, CF-1..CF-4); do not parse the digits after the hyphen, because HF-n and CF-n are different people. After the fix every person has exactly one sample and the project has no follow-up.
projects.affected_samples: all 9 samples; the four colliding pairs are HF-1/CF-1, HF-2/CF-2, HF-3/CF-3 and HF-4/CF-4

projects.issues_checked: Per-person follow-up of 20.0 y with a 365-day collection span (134 samples, 69 'people'; all values route R1, dates year-only). No negative, >110 y or pre-1990 values.
projects.cause: A single subject's two BioSamples disagree on age. Host subject id C0010 has a stool sample CG10 (SAMEA7232963) with host age 50 and a saliva sample CS10 (SAMEA7232987) with host age 30; sex (female), ethnicity (Indian), country and collection year (2018) are identical, and the pairing is the study's design (one gut plus one oral sample per subject). 66 of the 67 host subject ids in the project have a single consistent age across their pair, so this is one transcription error rather than a grouping fault. Neither the archive nor the two linked papers say which value is right -- the paper reports only group means (healthy controls mean age 40, range 21-66), and both 30 and 50 fall inside that range.
projects.correction_rule: clear age_at_collection_days for the two samples of host subject id C0010 in PRJEB39813 (SAMEA7232963 host age 50, SAMEA7232987 host age 30 -- irreconcilable). Keep 'host subject id' as the person key and leave the other 66 subjects unchanged. More generally, where a subject's gut and oral samples from the same year give different host age, clear rather than pick.

declared_limitations: PRJEB1220 and PRJEB29373 verdicts are provisional: both take their ages from supplementary tables in closed-access papers (Nielsen 2014 doi 10.1038/nbt.2939; Zhou 2020 PMID 31806420) that Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar, PMC and Crossref TDM all failed to return, so which of the two conflicting ages is correct could not be established and the grouping call rests on inference from archive naming patterns.

Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 on three attempts for PMC12353604 (PRJNA1169096), PMC6411461 (PRJNA419524), PMC12875530 (PRJEB83236) and PMC13727155 (PRJEB38909), and the PMC open-access S3 bucket held none of them; PRJNA419524 was covered by a second paper (PMC11209621) and the other three rest on archive records only.
No publication could be found in Europe PMC for PRJEB55648, PRJEB59450 or PRJNA1300398; those three verdicts rest on the archive records only.
PRJEB101630's replacement age for SAMEA120472561 is interpolated from the subject's other nine timepoints, not read from Supplementary Table S1, which was not retrieved.
PRJEB38909's person grouping could not be checked against the archive: the catalogued subject ids ('10509', 'F0164') appear in no ENA sample, run or experiment record.
